Definition: properly, cypress-resin; by analogy, sulphur (as equally inflammable)
BiblicalUsage: The word gophrîyth carries the sense of brimstone, sulphur. In Genesis 19:24, the text says "Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven." In Deuteronomy 29:23, the text says "And that] the whole land thereof [is] brimstone."
TheologicalSignificance: What gophrîyth teaches me is that God's judgment is just, and it falls where it should — no one escapes it, and no one suffers it unjustly. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
